description: We are Team Radical! We love beatboxing, music production, and noise!
summary: Project Radical developed a bridge for blind, low-vision, and curious explorers who want to hear how light pollution is changing throughout the world. Our song is made by analyzing 7 frames of SVS 5313 with 5 variables, Vibrancy, Happiness, Uniqueness, Contrast, and Column Average color vs Main color. By analyzing SVS 5313 with these 5 variables, we are able to convey the evolution of light pollution through harmonious tunes. Additionally, we allow explorers to swap the instruments used in the song on our website, in order to create the link that enables explorers to understand changes in our planet in the most pleasant sounding way possible. The link that we create is important because it goes beyond turning images into sound. Our team, Radical Changes, unlocks multi-modal awareness that fosters a deeper understanding of the changing world around us. Instead of having blindness or low-vision being a barrier to perception, Radical Changes turns it into a superpower. Every note, key strike, and pluck of a string is a genuine attempt to communicate the radical changes of the world around us and to unify explorers under the shared umbrella of curiosity.
details: Our algorithm analyzes 5 variables in 7 frames of Nasa's SVS 5313 video on the changes of light pollution in 3 second intervals in order to articulate our song. Main color (the overall color of the image) compared to each column's average color), this controls the melody. Vibrancy (dictated by a mix of saturation and brightness), this controls tempo, the higher the vibrancy, the higher the tempo, and vice versa. Happiness (100 minus the percentage of fully lit pixels), the more fully lit pixels, the more light pollution, therefore the less the happiness, vice versa for this one too. Uniqueness (a bright spot vs the light around it), at or over a score of 50 means shorter notes, under 50 means longer notes. Finally, Contrast (comparison between full-brightness and dark pixels), this picks the instruments. Our intended impact was to turn blindness and low-vision into a superpower that allows for a superior understanding of the changing world around us. We used python, JavaScript, Java, HTML, and CSS in our project. We also created an interactive website that allowed users to choose the instruments that allowed them best to understand our changing world. How project combined my software and coding expertise with my partner's extensive knowledge in music and sound production. We brainstormed innovative ways to communicate changes in data in the form of a harmonious song. We were able to boil down the most important factors in communicating change to the 5 variables mentioned above.
